# technical_se { #falconage.technical_se }

```python
technical_se(result, data=None, *, source='auto', icc=None, registry=None)
```

Standard error on each score attributable to assay measurement noise.

## Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name   | Type              | Description                                                                                                                                                        | Default    |
|--------|-------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------|
| result |                   | A :class:`~falconage.score.FalconResult`.                                                                                                                          | _required_ |
| data   |                   | The :class:`~falconage.core.FalconData` that was scored. Required for ``source="probe"``; the per-feature spread has to come from the matrix, not from the scores. | `None`     |
| source | str               | ``"probe"``, ``"clock"``, or ``"auto"`` (probe where possible, clock otherwise, and a recorded refusal where neither is available).                                | `'auto'`   |
| icc    | pd.Series \| None | Per-feature ICC, overriding the bundled table. Pass the output of :func:`icc_from_replicates` to use your own duplicates.                                          | `None`     |

## Notes {.doc-section .doc-section-notes}

An imputed feature contributes its **full** between-sample variance rather
than the reduced ``s²(1-ICC)``. This is deliberate and it is the part of the
calculation most likely to look wrong: an imputed value is the cohort mean
or a published reference, so it carries no information about the sample in
front of you, and treating it as a well-measured probe would make the
interval *narrower* for worse data.
